title: Techwear Without Looking Like You're in Costume
description: Techwear photographs great and reads weird on the street. Three rules — one technical piece, muted colour, the right shoes — that keep it wearable.
excerpt: Techwear is the fastest way to look like a sci-fi extra. Or like someone with a really good jacket. The difference is dosage.
content:
Techwear has one problem: it looks epic in photos and like a costume in real life. Straps, buckles, cords, pockets on pockets — wear it all at once and people remember you for the wrong reasons. Three rules fix it.

## One technical piece, everything else boring

Pick exactly one item that screams "tech" — a jacket with taped seams, trousers with a strap, a utility vest. Keep everything around it plain: a smooth tee, a basic hoodie, simple pants. Technical jacket plus technical pants plus a tactical sling bag stops being style and starts being a uniform.

## Colour: all-black is a trap, not a solution

Head-to-toe black is the shortcut to looking like event security. Try charcoal, deep olive, steel blue, or plain ecru instead. The best trick is the dullest one: a lighter top layer over a darker bottom removes half the operational vibe instantly. If you do want all black, break it with texture — matte jacket, glossy pants.

## Shoes decide whether you get away with it

This is where most fits collapse. Tall tactical boots plus a technical jacket equals costume. Go with a chunky everyday sneaker, a low work boot, or a clean runner silhouette instead. The shoe is what says "going into town" rather than "going on a mission."

Techwear works when nobody clocks it immediately but everybody notices it fits you. For a curated streetwear selection to pull that one piece from, check [DOPESTORE](https://dopestore.cz). And if you film your fits, [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) dubs the videos into dozens of languages, so people who don't speak your language still see them.
